steps.title: Get the motor
steps.hint: Look at the hardwareMap.get docs if you're stuck. The device name must match the robot config exactly.

content.value: The hardwareMap is an object that gives you access to every device attached to your robot. In your OpMode's runOpMode() method, call hardwareMap.get() to retrieve a motor by name. The name must match what is in the robot configuration.

steps.title: Power it on
steps.hint: setPower takes a value from -1.0 (full reverse) to 1.0 (full forward). Use 0.5 for half speed forward.

content.value: Once you have a reference to the motor, call setPower() to make it spin. The value ranges from -1.0 (full reverse) to 1.0 (full forward). Call this inside the while (opModeIsActive()) loop so it keeps running.

steps.title: Watch the encoder
steps.hint: getCurrentPosition() returns the number of encoder ticks since the last reset. Keep the motor running and the ticks will accumulate.

content.value: DC motors have built-in encoders that count rotation ticks. You can read the current count with getCurrentPosition(). Use telemetry to display the value on screen while the OpMode runs.

steps.title: Stop the motor
steps.hint: Always set power to 0.0 at the end of your OpMode. If you skip this, the motor keeps running after the OpMode stops.

content.value: When your OpMode ends, always set motor power to 0.0. Leaving motors at non-zero power can damage hardware and is against safe robot design rules. Add this after your while loop exits.
